text:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: After rolling fw v2.14.0 to ap-east-1 OOB controllers we are seeing repeated UART packet-loss and IPMI session failures on ~18 hosts. Provisioning and deprovision jobs are timing out.

maya: seeing the same. GPU pool for gpu-large-ap-east has 12 nodes in 'drain' and autoscaler keeps trying to replace, hitting quota and racking up cost. Can we stop new replacements?

youssef: pausing autoscaler now (scaledown disabled). also throttling provisioning queue.

kevin: @maya @youssef do we have recent BMC logs? suspect the fw changed UART baud/flow settings.

maya: pasted a short log from a failing host: ```
Apr 12 03:14:02 bmc uart0: rx err=5 dropped=23
Apr 12 03:14:04 ipmi: session 0x3f aborted: transport error
Apr 12 03:14:06 kernel: console [ttyS0] hang: fifo overrun
```

lina: also noticed secureboot flag flipped to 'enabled' on some nodes after the update, which explains unreachable nodes during PXE handoff. only in ap-east-1-rack7 so far.

youssef: confirmed. secureboot toggle appears to be a side-effect of the bootrom rewrite step. Need to run a validation step to prevent toggle.

kevin: urgent mitigation plan: 1) pause further firmware rollout, 2) queue targeted BMC reboots for affected hosts (serial-over-LAN reset), 3) mark the rack as no-provision until vendor patch. Anyone object?

maya: +1 do it. Also we should route new scale requests to eu-west temporarily to avoid cost shock on ap-east reserved pool.

infra-bot: ACTION: autoscaler paused by youssef at 2076543350. Bulk reprovisioning suspended.

youssef: running an ipmitool reset on a test host now: ```
# ipmitool -H 10.0.72.19 -U admin -P **** chassis power cycle
Sent power control command: cycle
```

maya: after soft reset, serial improves but still sporadic packet loss. vendor-support-bot, opening a ticket with the vendor, include logs and sample serial dump.

vendor-support-bot: Ticket #VND-98712 created with vendor. ETA preliminary triage 4 hours.

kevin: we should also add a temporary prefix-cache bypass for provisioning to reduce the number of IPMI sessions. low-risk config: ```
provisioning: 
  ipmi_concurrency: 4  # lowered from 12
  serial_timeout_ms: 120000
```

lina: added the config change to staging, rolling to production in 5m. This should reduce simultaneous BMC load.

maya: cost note: because replacements kept starting then failing, billing shows a short spike in reserved GPU consumption. finance flagged an alert. We need to reconcile hours and escalate to sales for customers that may be impacted.

youssef: capturing all affected instance IDs and tagnames, will push to a billing incident doc and add to the vendor ticket.

kevin: if vendor can't patch quickly, fallback is to roll back fw on remaining racks to v2.13.3 and run a canary on one rack. rollback runbook: ```
for host in $(cat affected_hosts); do 
  scp fw_v2.13.3.bin root@${host}:/tmp && ipmitool -H $host -U admin -P p -- raw 0x0 0x1 0x2
done
```
Do not run in parallel on >2 hosts at once.

maya: agreed. also add a verification step to check secureboot state before bringing host back into pool: `redwoodctl host inspect --secureboot`

lina: I'm monitoring telemetry and will post periodic updates. current affected count: 18 hosts, 6 in drain, 12 unhealthy.

vendor-support-bot: Vendor initial triage: "We see UART framing errors introduced by the bootrom rewrite on specific ASPEED revisions. Reproducible in lab. Working on rollback patch and a fw diff to skip secureboot flag toggles."

kevin: good. once vendor provides patch we will: 1) apply to canary rack 2) run serial loop test for 2 hours 3) gradual rollout with monitoring thresholds. set rollout throttle to 1 rack per 45m.

maya: noted. I'll coordinate on customer comms and raise a short incident postmortem draft once we stabilise.

infra-bot: UPDATE: autoscaler resumed for non-ap-east regions only at 2076544120.

lina: last update before vendor fix: we disabled live replacements for the ap-east GPU pool and routed scale to eu-west. billing reconcile started (work item W-1543).

kevin: thanks team. keep updates here. if anyone sees a node flip secureboot back to enabled unexpectedly, call it out immediately. :thumbsup:
